goal_title: Book: Foundations Crisis: The Limits of Formalization — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in foundationscrisis became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.

book.title: Foundations Crisis: The Limits of Formalization

reading.arc: Foundations Crisis walks one habit through seven materials and then turns it on the project itself: find the instrument, read what it actually measures, and name the gap between that and its caption. Euclid's hall plants the method in a plaque whose gold arrives before the argument and a triangle that prints sixties it never measured; NonEuclid changes the host and makes 180 degrees one answer among three; Russell withdraws the permission to collect everything; Godel separates a stopped search from a proof that no search can succeed. Escher moves the question into where you stand, Brouwer into what you have made versus what you assert about every continuation, Florensky into what follows when reports conflict and who still gets through. Crisis_Synthesis brings in the QFEP formula as a sentence with handles and applies the sequence's habit to it (colour on a rail is a proposal, a total can hide its compensations) before handing the lit formula to the laboratory. The stance is consistent and rare: every apparatus is described as smaller than its claim, and the prose treats that as the lesson rather than an apology.
holds: The refrain 'what did this number depend on?': each hall ends on an instrument that measures less than its caption (three sixties, a stopped prover arm, a move counter, a flickering lamp, complementary opacities, a finite orbit sample), and the prose names the shortfall every time instead of hiding it.

Carried works, all confirmed in the map layers: the triangle (Euclid -> NonEuclid -> Brouwer), the parallel lines (Euclid -> Brouwer), the postulates plaque (Euclid -> Russell), and in Synthesis the Russell workbench, the set box, the staircase, the sphere and the Godel plaque return.

The distinction handed in from GT_Matching (a procedure meeting its local rule is not a proof of its strongest advertised conclusion) recurs as the prover that jams, the prefix that proves nothing about every continuation, the diagonal that displays no completed infinity, the counter that 'does not prove chaos'.
The small verbatim excerpt as the whole of an apparatus: `% 5`, two Booleans, `terms.append(value)`, `_d[i] = 1 - _list[i][i]`, `x = r * x * (1.0 - x)`, each used the same way: this is all it does.
Closings on the body and the floor: 'The floor has not moved. Your account of it has.'; 'You are allowed to leave it.'; 'It has made a small part wait for it.'
Each last paragraph names the next hall's question, so the reader crosses every threshold knowing what to ask.

hall_notes.note: Seven numbered sections read the build: the plaque's `% 5` loop and its gold branch, three unevenly spaced lines, a triangle labelled 60/60/60 that measures 53.1/63.4/63.4, a screen drawing a grid before anything arrives. Reads as a code-reading essay addressed to a walker, the longest chapter in the arc, and the one whose register slips most between 'Walk between the columns' and 'In the source, move Line3'.

The bench's HOST slider (PLANE / SPHERE / DISK) rebuilds a triangle per host and asks its corners; Gauss-Bonnet is named and held at arm's length ('one changing display is not a proof'). Reads cleanly and ends on the sequence's best closing line; the side works are described faithfully except the curvature slider, which ships as a number readout, not a surface sketch.

IN / OUT at cell 5, then 'within U' at cell 6; the box, braces, barber, liar and hotel are sorted into contradiction versus offended expectation. The argument is precise and the two-Boolean excerpt is the code; the floor texts (IF IT DOES / IT DOESN'T) go unmentioned but do no harm.

A stopped prover arm and a sorter with a gold gap; the prose is careful (three kinds of failed search, soundness named) but anchors two of ten placed works, wears a different template (H1, question line, no sections, inline link) and is a third the length of its neighbours. The floor slogans say what the chapter asks the reader not to say yet.

STEP around a tabletop model whose console adds up ascent and descent; FORM cycles five constructions (RETURN SIDE, CLOSING DROP, OPEN RUN, SCAFFOLD, TILTED TREADS); then the green bead at the Penrose beams and the trident's two-into-three. Every control, name and number checks against escher_staircase_study.gd; the most physically grounded hall in the arc.

'Wait before touching anything': two buttons append to a prefix the program has not stored ahead; excluded middle as a reading slider; the sqrt2^sqrt2 case split; Cantor's finite diagonal; a timed staircase for contrast. Faithful to code (256 / 10 / 32 bits, blue and amber beads); the one slip is 'nearby' for a work at the other end of the hall.

Walk through a closed leaf; three buttons hold P and not-P without the alarm following; the sphere keeps A and not-A; the two quantum toys at the back are refused as certificates. Strong on non-explosion versus dialetheism; the Schrodinger paragraph is written from a desk.

The formula with three reading buttons and two disputed rails; the logistic map under its own r; the atrium's 1:10 model; five returning works; a closing turn to whose possibilities an arrangement sustains. As source it is the arc's best synthesis; as rendered, an unclosed code fence swallows its second half and all three footnotes.

stumbles: Crisis_Synthesis: the code fence at line 43 is two backticks, so everything after `x = r * x * (1.0 - x)` (atrium, returning works, closing section, three footnotes) renders as one monospace block.

Godel_Incompleteness: 443 words for a hall of ten works; eight pass without a sentence, and the floor under the visitor says 'SELF-REFERENCE IS THE EDGE' three rooms after Russell called that lesson too thin.

Euclid_Parallel section 6: 'So we open on the fallback: `_point_mode = true`' describes a scan this map never runs; the token `#mode:grid` sets GRID VIEW explicitly and the screen draws sixteen by sixteen empty cells.
Florensky_Paraconsistent: 'on a desktop click, a randomly chosen ALIVE or DEAD result' is a desktop aside; in the headset the box's input handler returns and the lid never opens.
Crisis_Synthesis: the first sentence, 'A formula waits in the next room', is read while standing four cells from the formula.

NonEuclidean_Spaces: 'changes its own surface sketch' for a slider placed without a witness token, which builds no surface; and the heading 'The surfaces beside the bench' for works at the far end of the hall.
Brouwer_Intuitionism: 'The nearby sum over hypotheses' after the triangle and lines at the back, for a work standing beside the choice bench at the front.
Euclid_Parallel: 'In the source, move Line3's offset out to 0.4' asks a visitor to edit a scene file; 'three placements ship them' counts corridor and test copies; 'isoceles'.
Crisis_Synthesis: 'The plaque, the nested box and the staircase return as reminders', but the Godel plaque was never introduced, so for the reader it appears here for the first time.

keep.quote: Count once more: five postulates, three lines, one triangle, one screen, two rows of pillars. Every number is true. Not one of them is necessary.
For now, return the slider to PLANE. The floor has not moved. Your account of it has.
The arrows turn around the same disc. Your hand has somewhere to go; the proposed set does not.
That matters because a slow search, a broken search and a proof that no search can succeed are three different things.
The mark offers a place from which to believe the image. You are allowed to leave it. What else becomes convincing only when we remain in the assigned place?
This room has not made the world obey your hand. It has made a small part wait for it.
The visible assertion "closed" has no authority to stop you. Someone had to make that decision. A system can preserve conflicting descriptions and still have to decide who gets through.
The earlier rooms have not proved it. An equals sign can gather a desire before we know how to measure it.

reading.handover_in: GT_Matching ends by naming the foundations sequence and handing over one distinction: a procedure meeting its local rule is not automatically a proof of its strongest advertised conclusion. Euclid_Parallel never repeats the phrase, but its whole method is that distinction applied (the plaque's gold branch, the triangle's shipped sixties, the screen's grid before data) and its last lines answer it directly ('Every number is true. Not one of them is necessary'). The join is clean if implicit; the only friction is register: the reader leaves a 574-word hall with one control and enters a 1709-word hall with seven code excerpts and instructions that sometimes address an editor rather than a walker.
reading.handover_out: Crisis_Synthesis ends 'Leave the formula lit. We will meet it again in the laboratory, where particular implementations give its terms consequences', and QFEP_Introduction opens 'In the previous room, the formula waited to be questioned. Here it returns a number'. A clean pass; QFEP_Introduction even corrects an expectation Crisis sets ('Move phi through zero') by noting its own phi rail is nonnegative. Two wrinkles on the Crisis side: its opening line 'A formula waits in the next room' belongs to Florensky's exit, not this hall's entrance, and its unclosed code fence means the reader arrives at the laboratory having read the synthesis's second half as monospace.
